subject: FastRetail trial kickoff - workload intake, success criteria, and traffic sync
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Novak <claire.novak@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T15:18:00-08:00
Subject: FastRetail discovery recap & workload intake (next steps)

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can scope the POC effectively. I captured what you shared and added a few clarifying questions. Please correct anything I got wrong.

High-level goal
- Validate Redwood can meet FastRetail’s low-latency personalization endpoint for customer-facing product recommendations at production-like traffic.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end < 700 ms for 99% of requests during steady-state.
- Throughput: sustain 120 RPS steady-state for the catalog personalization endpoint.
- Burst: tolerate short bursts up to ~800 RPS for 60–120 seconds (expected peak during marketing blasts).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~30–50 active requests; occasional spikes to 200 concurrent during peak windows.
- Output quality: top-3 recommendation relevance TTL A/B test lift >= 8% over baseline.

Workload details we need (attached a starter CSV):
- RPS by endpoint (steady / peak / scheduled bursts)
- Typical request token length (median and 90th) and expected generation length
- Concurrency distribution over 24h and expected burst cadence (times/duration)
- Authentication method for test keys (IP allowlist / bearer) and any rate-limiters in front of our load generator

From today’s call my notes on tokens: you estimated request payloads around 60–90 tokens (median ~75); response generation avg ~180–220 tokens for personalization output. If you can provide histograms that will help kernel selection and batching configs.

Attachments: fastretail_workload_intake.csv — please populate the shaded columns and attach a small sample of production logs (anonymized) if possible.

Proposed owners & timeline
- FastRetail: Claire (product) + Mike (platform) — provide intake CSV and sample logs by EOD Wednesday 12/9.
- Redwood: Soojin (sales/solutions) + Ben (capacity & infra) — propose test window, generate test keys, and prepare Dedicated/Hosted capacity notes by end of week.
- Kickoff: schedule POC kickoff the week of 12/14; propose 60-minute session for environment walk-through and success criteria alignment.

Open questions
1) Can you confirm whether requests will include session-level KV or external context that needs prefix caching? If yes, share cache hit expectations.
2) Any regulatory requirements around log retention or token redaction we should consider?
3) Are you able to provide a 1–2 hour maintenance window in the first 2 weeks of the POC for kernel/quantization experiments?

Next steps
- Claire: fill the attached CSV + send a sample anonymized log.
- Ben: I’ve looped Ben for capacity recommendations — he’ll propose a plan for steady-state vs reserved throughput.
- I'll send calendar invites for a kickoff once we have the intake back.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Claire Novak <claire.novak@fastretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mike Brown <mike.brown@fastretail.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail discovery recap & workload intake (next steps)

Thanks Soojin — this looks right and very helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Token lengths: median request ~70, 95th percentile ~120. Response length median ~190 tokens. We’ll confirm exact histograms but those numbers align with our sampling.
- Bursts: marketing campaigns cause predictable bursts roughly 2–3 times/day for 60–90s; sometimes a single campaign will produce a sustained higher burst (~4–5 minutes) but that’s less frequent.

Forwarding this to Mike (platform) — Mike will help with anonymized log export and how quickly we can get you a test key.

On the KV/cache question: we do include session-level user context (small blobs ~1–2KB) that are often identical for returning sessions. Cache hit rate expected ~65% on average.

We’ll try to get the filled CSV and a small (anonymized) log dump by EOD Wednesday 12/9. If anything slips, we’ll let you know.

- Claire

On Thu, Dec 5, 2026 at 3:18 PM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:

Subject: Redwood capacity note for FastRetail POC

Hi all — looping in a couple of practical notes from the infra side based on the traffic profile in Soojin’s recap and Claire’s clarifications.

Short summary
- For steady 120 RPS with ~75 token requests / ~200 token responses, we recommend starting on a 3-GPU Dedicated pool (A100/RTX class equivalent) with autoscale headroom to cover bursts.
- If FastRetail prefers Hosted to avoid reserved commits, we can run the POC on Hosted with burst credits and a conservative autoscale policy; expect slightly higher unit cost but faster ramp.

Specifics we’ll validate during POC prep
- Prefix/KV cache behavior: with 65% hit rate, we can tune batch sizes and cache affinity to reduce end-to-end token cost by ~20%.
- Warm-up: recommend a 30–45 minute warm-up (low steady traffic ramp) before any measured run to populate KV caches and get stable latency.
- Burst testing: we can reproduce 800 RPS bursts for 90s safely in a staging environment; we’ll need a maintenance window if you want us to push longer sustained bursts.

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_proposal.pdf (proposal with cost estimates and scale knobs).

Proposed test window
- Option A: 12/15 09:00–11:00 PT — steady run with two staged bursts (90s each).
- Option B: 12/16 15:00–17:00 PT — extended burst tolerance test with shorter warm-up.

Can you confirm preferred window and whether you want Hosted or Dedicated trial? Ben will draft the low-level runbook once we confirm.

Thanks — Ben

Ben Carter
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks Ben and Claire — perfect.

I’ll prepare a kickoff invite for one of the two proposed windows and include a short runbook draft and test checklist ahead of time. Action items consolidated below:

Action owners calendar

- Ben (Redwood): review logs, produce a draft runbook (warm-up, measurement hooks, fallback policies) and cost estimate (Hosted vs Dedicated) by 12/11.
- Soojin (Redwood): send kickoff invite and provide Drive folder with test scripts and a pre-filled runbook template by 12/10.

Kickoff agenda (60 min)
1) Introductions & scope confirmation (10 min)
2) Review success criteria and acceptance gates (10 min)
3) Walk through workload intake and sample logs (15 min)
4) Test run plan: warm-up, steady-state, bursts, teardown (15 min)
5) Next steps & ownership (10 min)

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bFastRetail-POC (I’ll populate with runbook and scripts).

If that all looks good I’ll tentatively block Option A (12/15 09:00 PT) and share invites — Claire, let me know if you need a different slot.

—
Soojin
